examples.en: The ancient history lesson started in history class.
Ancient history is hard but fun.
There is still much unknown in ancient history.

examples.ko: 고대사를 공부하려면 옛 기록을 읽어야 해요.
examples.en: To study ancient history, you have to read old records.
My younger sibling is very interested in ancient history.
That scholar studies the secrets of ancient history.

explain: 한국사에서 '고대'는 보통 삼국 시대와 통일신라 무렵까지를 말해요. '중세사', '근대사', '현대사'와 나란히 시대를 나눌 때 써요. 학교 역사 수업과 교과서에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I'm very interested in ancient Korean history.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라 이름을 앞에 붙여서 어느 나라의 고대사인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a country name before it to say whose ancient history.

phrases.en: I'm studying ancient history at university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학문이나 전공을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about a subject or major.

phrases.en: I borrowed an ancient history book from the library.

explain_en: In Korean history, 고대 usually means up to the Three Kingdoms and Unified Silla period. It is used alongside 중세사, 근대사, and 현대사 when dividing eras. It appears often in school history classes and textbooks.

examples.en: These days, domestic products are of very good quality too.
My grandmother tries to use only domestic products.
There's a poster urging people to use domestic products.
Domestic products are cheaper than foreign ones.
This shop specializes in domestic products.
I chose a domestic product as a gift.

explain: 우리나라에서 만든 물건을 말하고, 반대말은 '수입품'이에요. '국산품 애용'은 오래전부터 쓰던 표어 같은 말이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '국산'이라고 하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: This bag is made in Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '국산품'을 줄인 말로 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 국산품, used more in daily speech.

phrases.en: I use domestic products whenever I can.
phrases.nuance_ko: '애용하다'는 즐겨 자주 쓴다는 뜻이고, 오래된 표어에도 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: 애용하다 means to use regularly; it also appears in old slogans.

phrases.en: I compared the prices of domestic and imported goods.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with its opposite, 수입품.

explain_en: It means goods made in Korea, and the opposite is '수입품'. '국산품 애용' is a long-used slogan-like phrase. In daily talk people often just say '국산'.

en: very first time; first time in one's life

examples.en: I rode an airplane for the first time in my life.
I went on a trip alone for the first time in my life.
It was food I had never seen before, so I was a bit scared.
I came first for the very first time and was really happy.

examples.ko: 저는 난생처음 김치를 직접 담가 봤어요.
examples.en: I made kimchi by myself for the first time in my life.

examples.ko: 난생처음 겪는 일이라 어떻게 해야 할지 몰랐어요.
examples.en: It was my first experience ever, so I didn't know what to do.

explain: 그냥 '처음'이 아니라 태어나서 지금까지 한 번도 없었다는 놀라움을 강조해요. 보통 '난생처음 + 동사'처럼 부사처럼 바로 동사 앞에 쓰고, '생전 처음'도 비슷하게 말해요.

phrases.en: I saw the sea for the first time in my life.
phrases.nuance_ko: '난생처음'과 뜻은 같고, '으로'를 붙여 뒤의 동사와 이어서 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '난생처음'; adding '으로' just links it to the verb that follows.
phrases.en_equiv: for the first time in my life

phrases.en: I wore a hanbok for the first time ever.
phrases.nuance_ko: '난생처음'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 말할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same meaning as the headword, common in speech.

phrases.en: It's my first time ever doing this, so I'm nervous.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'와 함께 첫 경험을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Combined with '-아/어 보다' to talk about a first-time experience.
phrases.en_equiv: to try for the first time in one's life

explain_en: Rather than a plain 'first', it stresses surprise that this has never happened since you were born. It usually sits right before a verb like an adverb, and '생전 처음' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: When night fell, the neon lights on the street came on.
Myeongdong is full of flashy neon lights.
We made the shop name into a neon sign.
I took a photo under the neon lights.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에는 네온이 길에 비쳐서 예뻐요.
examples.en: On rainy days, the neon reflects on the road and looks pretty.

examples.ko: 저 가게 네온은 고장 났는지 깜빡거려요.
examples.en: The neon at that shop is flickering, maybe because it's broken.

explain: '네온'은 원래 기체 이름이지만 일상에서는 밤거리의 네온 불빛이나 간판을 가리킬 때가 많아요. 보통 '네온사인', '네온 간판'으로 더 자주 말해요. 불이 '켜지다', '꺼지다'와 같이 써요.

phrases.en: The neon sign in front of the shop is sparkling.
phrases.nuance_en: A more common everyday word than plain 네온.

phrases.en: At night the neon signboards look very pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게 이름을 알리는 간판일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it is a signboard showing a shop's name.

phrases.en: When the sun sets, the neon lights come on.
phrases.nuance_en: Lights go with 켜지다 and 꺼지다.

explain_en: 네온 is originally the name of a gas, but in daily speech it usually means the glowing lights or signs seen on night streets. People more often say 네온사인 or 네온 간판. It goes with 켜지다 and 꺼지다.

examples.en: Someone is clattering dishes in the kitchen.

examples.ko: 밤새 창문이 달그락거려서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The window rattled all night, so I couldn't sleep.
Mom is washing dishes with a clatter.
I can hear coins clinking in the pocket.
The keys in the drawer rattled.
Carry the dishes carefully so they don't clatter.

explain: 그릇, 숟가락, 동전처럼 작고 단단한 물건이 부딪히는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. '덜그럭거리다'는 좀 더 크고 무거운 느낌이에요. '달그락달그락'처럼 반복해서 소리를 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: I heard a clattering sound at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 '소리'를 붙여서 들린 소리를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'sound' lets you describe what you heard.

phrases.example: 동전이 가방 안에서 달그락달그락 소리가 나요.
phrases.en: The coins rattle in my bag.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the repeated form that imitates the sound.

phrases.en: The baby is sleeping, so please don't clatter the dishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 내지 말라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask someone not to make that noise.

explain_en: It imitates the sound of small hard things like bowls, spoons or coins knocking together. '덜그럭거리다' feels a bit bigger and heavier. People also repeat it as '달그락달그락' to describe the sound.

en: yahoo; woo-hoo (a cheer, or a shout on a mountain)

examples.en: At the top of the mountain I shouted "yahoo" loudly.
Yay! It's finally vacation!

examples.ko: 아이들은 눈을 보고 야호 하며 뛰어나갔어요.
examples.en: Seeing the snow, the kids ran out cheering.
The exam was over, so everyone cheered.
The shout echoed in the mountains.

examples.ko: 동생이 선물을 받고 야호 하고 좋아했어요.
examples.en: My little brother got a gift and cheered happily.

explain: '야호'는 기쁠 때 내는 소리이고, 특히 등산하다가 산 위에서 외치는 소리로 유명해요. 요즘은 산에서 소리를 지르는 것을 조심하라고 해서 예전만큼 많이 하지는 않아요. 기뻐서 외칠 때는 '앗싸'나 '만세'도 써요.

phrases.example: 친구들과 산 위에서 야호 하고 외쳤어요.
phrases.en: My friends and I shouted "yahoo" on top of the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '야호'를 소리 내어 말할 때 '하고 외치다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '하고 외치다' to say someone shouted 야호 out loud.

phrases.nuance_ko: 기쁜 일이 생겼을 때 친구끼리 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual cheer for friends when something good happens.

phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 기뻐하며 두 손을 들 때 외치는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shouted with joy, often with both hands raised.

explain_en: 야호 is a sound of joy, and it is especially famous as the shout from a mountaintop while hiking. Today people are asked not to shout in the mountains, so it is done less than before. For a joyful cheer you can also say 앗싸 or 만세.
